question: What is the primary goal of the National Programme on Immunization?

options.A: Treating chronic non-communicable illnesses in adults
options.B: Supplying essential nutrition supplements to pregnant women
options.D: Providing free surgical care for newborn congenital defects

explanation: The NPI focuses specifically on preventing infectious diseases through safe and effective vaccination schedules. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: Why did Nigeria adopt the Expanded Programme on Immunization framework?

options.A: To replace traditional herbal medicine practitioners entirely
options.B: To generate revenue for local government health clinics
options.C: To combat high rates of preventable childhood mortality
options.D: To manage emergency trauma cases from road traffic accidents

explanation: The initiative was localized to address and lower the heavy burden of death caused by infectious childhood diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: Which vaccines are typically given to a newborn baby immediately at birth?
explanation: Newborns receive BCG for tuberculosis protection and OPV zero right at birth before leaving the health facility. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h2)

question: An infant is brought to the clinic at 14 weeks old with no previous shots. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the mother to return when the child reaches one year of age
options.B: Wait until the child is two years old before starting any injections
options.C: Administer catch-up doses according to the national guidelines
options.D: Give only the birth vaccines since the infant missed the early schedule

explanation: Don't worry if a baby comes in late! Just use national catch-up guidelines to get them protected as safely and quickly as possible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain system?

options.A: Transporting medical personnel safely to remote rural outposts
options.B: Preventing theft of expensive pharmaceutical supplies in storage
options.C: Freezing needles and syringes to sterilize them before use
options.D: Keeping vaccines at the correct temperature to preserve their potency

explanation: Biological vaccines are sensitive to heat and require strict temperature controls to remain effective against diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h3)

question: What does a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) tell you?

options.A: The exact number of doses remaining inside the glass vial
options.B: Whether heat exposure has damaged the vaccine's potency
options.C: Whether the vaccine container has been contaminated with bacteria
options.D: The precise manufacturing date printed on the cardboard box

explanation: Think of the VVM as a heat-watchdog! It changes color when exposed to too much heat, letting you know if the vaccine is still safe to use. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h3)

question: Why is documenting vaccine administration in the child health card important?

options.A: It creates an accurate health record to guide future clinical care
options.B: It acts as a legal receipt for fees paid at the clinic counter
options.C: It proves to the government that the nurse worked a full shift
options.D: It prevents mothers from visiting any other health facility ever again

explanation: Clear documentation ensures subsequent providers know which doses were given and when the next ones are due. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: A mother is scared that immunization injections will make her baby sick. How should you respond?

options.A: Scold her for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Explain normal mild side effects and reassure her about the benefits
options.C: Advise her to skip the injections entirely if she feels worried
options.D: Tell her that children never experience any discomfort from vaccines

explanation: Moms often worry! Taking a moment to calmly explain normal side effects like low fever builds great trust and helps keep babies on schedule. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: What does the term AEFI stand for in public health nursing?
explanation: AEFI is the standard global acronym used to describe medical incidents occurring after a person receives a vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal, minor side effect after routine vaccination?

options.A: Mild low-grade fever lasting twenty-four hours
options.B: Temporary irritability and mild crying in an infant
options.C: Severe anaphylactic shock with airway closure
options.D: Slight swelling and tenderness at the injection site

explanation: Sore arms, slight fever, and fussiness are totally normal. Severe airway closure (anaphylaxis) is a rare medical emergency, not a routine side effect! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h5)

question: What is a major operational challenge to routine immunization coverage in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of refrigeration units in primary clinics
options.B: Geographic barriers and hard-to-reach rural settlements
options.C: Too many trained nurses available for community outreach
options.D: A complete absence of infectious diseases in the country

explanation: Getting vaccines across rivers, bad roads, and remote terrain to reach every single child is one of our biggest field challenges. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h6)

question: How can community leaders help improve low immunization uptake in rural areas?

options.A: By importing vaccines directly from international manufacturers
options.B: By taking over clinical duties and injecting vaccines themselves
options.C: By replacing the cold chain refrigerators with local coolers
options.D: By building trust and addressing local rumors or hesitancy

explanation: Local chiefs and religious leaders have powerful voices. When they support immunization, community members feel much more confident bringing their babies in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h6)
